info.name: Tada AI Normalization - Provider APIs (PrismHR, isolved, UKG Ready)
info.description:
Exploratory requests against the three take-home providers' live demo APIs, fronted by the organizer's demo-provider-signin service. Covers the four data types from the take-home: company/employee data, direct deposits, deductions, and payroll data.

Every request's Tests tab checks more than HTTP status: it verifies the body is JSON (not an HTML error page), checks PrismHR's embedded errorCode on responses that return 200 even on business errors, and asserts the documented response field actually contains the right shape of data. Run the whole collection with Postman's Collection Runner (or Newman) and the results view tells you exactly which provider/endpoint is broken and at which layer (auth, routing, or data).

Setup:
1. Import this collection and the companion environment file (Tada AI Normalization - Demo.postman_environment.json).
2. Select that environment in Postman's environment dropdown.
3. Set demo_signin_api_key to the key the organizer gave you privately (never commit it).
4. Run the three requests in '0 - Sign In' once - their Tests scripts populate every other variable this collection needs.
5. Run requests inside the PrismHR / isolved / UKG Ready folders top-to-bottom; each folder's early requests auto-save the ids its later requests depend on.

See postman/TESTING_FLOW.md in the repo for the full walkthrough, expected responses, token-refresh notes, and troubleshooting.

item.name: 0 - Sign In (run these first)
item.description: Obtains short-lived credentials from the organizer-provided demo-provider-signin service for each of the three tenants. Each request's Tests tab asserts the response shape explicitly (so a missing field fails loudly here instead of causing a confusing failure three requests later) and auto-saves the token, base_url, and demo company identifiers into this environment. Run all three once per session, and again whenever a token expires, before using the provider folders below.

item.name: PrismHR
item.description: All requests use sessionId as a header (set by the Sign In request) rather than Bearer auth. Spec: contracts/prismhr/openapi/prismhr-2025.09.openapi.json. Every PrismHR response wraps its payload with errorCode/errorMessage at the top level even on HTTP 200 - the tests below check that field, not just the HTTP status. Run 'Get Client List' then 'Get Employee List' first so prismhr_client_id and prismhr_employee_id are populated for the requests below.

item.name: isolved
item.description: Uses the primary isolved v6 swagger snapshot only (contracts/isolved/openapi/isolved-v6.swagger.json) - do not mix in the alternate snapshot's schemas. Auth is 'Authorization: Bearer <access_token>' from the Sign In request. Collection/list endpoints here (clients, employees, checks) return a paged wrapper with the items under '.results', not '.items' or a bare array - the tests below check '.results' specifically. Run 'Get Clients' and 'Get Legals' first if isolved_client_id/legal_id are not already set from sign-in.
